transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Time: 16:00 EST
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Riley (Redwood SE), Aisha (Montage Head of Search), Tom (ML Eng), Clara (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Short discovery on embeddings/reranking; focus on vector DB integration, throughput targets, dimensionality tradeoffs, and options for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Customer wants a pilot and a benchmark run.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros. I'm Jordan with Redwood, AE. Riley's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Aisha: Hi all, I'm Aisha, lead on search at Montage. We've got Tom and Clara with me. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Riley: Great, quick agenda — understand your current stack, volume and latency targets, talk embedding model and vector DB, then next steps and pilot plan. Sound good?
[00:28] Tom: Yep. We'll try to be quick, we've got a 45 minute window.
[00:35] Jordan: Cool. Aisha, can you give us 2 min on your current infra and what triggered evaluation of Redwood?
[00:42] Aisha: Sure. So Montage runs a product search and recommendation engine — mixes semantic search and classic keyword. Right now embeddings are generated by a small in-house model (2B variant) and we store vectors in Pinecone; we also have a fallback to OpenSearch for boolean filters. We're starting to hit latency at scale during peak — about 200 qps at peak with p95 around 230ms but when we do reranking with cross-encoder LTR it spikes. We're looking for better cost/latency tradeoffs and easier way to run rerankers and embedding infra; also considering private deployment because we have some regulated customers asking for data residency.
[01:18] Riley: When you say reranking, is that a separate cross-encoder call after retrieval?
[01:22] Tom: Yeah — retrieve top K (usually 100) then cross-encoder LTR on the 100. It's expensive and that's why we're worried about cost.
[01:30] Riley: Got it. Two quick clarifying q's — what dimensionality are your vectors and what's the cardinality of your index?
[01:36] Aisha: Right now 768 dims. About 2.1 million total vectors across product catalog and historical queries. We plan to grow to ~5M by year end.
[01:45] Jordan: Cool. And latency SLOs for search path?
[01:48] Aisha: P95 under 200ms we'd love; p50 under 60ms. For reranking it's okay up to 500ms but overall cost per query is a concern.
[01:58] Riley: Understood. On the hosting side, Redwood can run the whole pipeline hosted (our API), Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC/on-prem. For the use-case you described, common pattern is embeddings in-hosted with vector DB hosted by you, or we can host vector index with a partner — but many customers integrate Redwood outputs into Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus.
[02:22] Clara: For compliance we need SOC2 plus SSO and KMS integration. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:29] Jordan: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integrations and you can bring your own key in the Private offering. Hosted supports envelope encryption and we have SOC2 compliance. I'll share the security whitepaper.
[02:38] Riley: On the rerank cost, two levers we usually recommend: reduce top-K with a denser store or hybrid rerank (embedding-based lightweight rerank then cross-encoder only on very top), and model quantization to lower cost. Also batching for cross-encoder runs if you can accept a bit more latency.
[02:55] Tom: Hybrid rerank — can you explain more? We currently do simple cosine + PU weight and then feed to cross-encoder.
[03:02] Riley: Sure. Hybrid search here means we do ANN retrieval (FAISS/Pinecone) to get a candidate set, then an efficient embedding-based lightweight model to rerank (like a 200M dot-product model), then only run the heavy cross-encoder on top 10. That reduces calls to the big model by an order of magnitude. It's pretty standard. Some customers run the embedding similarity as a learned scorer in the vector DB too.
[03:25] Aisha: Oh ok. That would help. Our biggest constraint is throughput — during peak we need consistent 200 qps and bursts to 500 for black Friday style events. Can Redwood Dedicated handle that?
[03:36] Riley: Yes, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. We can configure autoscaling and burst capacity; SLA-backed latency targets are available. We'll dimension the pool based on your benchmark numbers. For hosted, we can often hit these numbers too but cost varies and you don't get BYOK KMS.
[03:51] Jordan: Important to know: Dedicated gives you isolation and more predictable per-token pricing. Private gives you network control, on-prem if needed. Hosted is fastest to get started.
[03:59] Clara: From infra perspective, how does Redwood integrate with our vector DB? We want to keep Pinecone and not migrate if possible.
[04:07] Riley: We commonly do this: Redwood produces embeddings through the API or via a private deployment; you push those vectors to Pinecone/Weaviate. Retrieval happens in Pinecone, then you call Redwood for reranking (we also support a rerank endpoint that accepts candidates and runs cross-encoder). Alternatively, deploy Redwood Private next to your vector store and do low-latency calls internally.
[04:28] Tom: Latency between services is a concern — our Pinecone is in us-east and you'd run in us-east as well?
[04:34] Riley: We have region options; for Hosted you can choose region. For Private it's co-located. For Dedicated we can place capacity in the same cloud region. Network latency should be single-digit ms if colocated.
[04:45] Aisha: What about dimensionality — we're at 768, should we move to 1024 or down to 384? What's the trade?
[04:52] Riley: Higher dims can improve representational capacity but increase storage and ANN recall costs. Many customers stick to 768 for transformer-based embeddings; if you need to compress, PCA or product quantization can reduce dims; alternatively, you can reduce dims and retrain the embedder. We also recommend evaluating recall vs latency with a held-out benchmark — we can run sweep of dims.
[05:12] Jordan: Also note quantized models on Dedicated can give 3-4x speedups with minimal quality loss depending on model. We'll provide quantization profiles.
[05:20] Tom: On throughput, any guidance on batch sizes for embedding generation? We have spikes and variable doc lengths.
[05:27] Riley: For embeddings, continuous batching in our runtime gives good throughput. Batch sizes depend on GPU and memory; we'll share recommended batch configs. For embeddings throughput, expect tens of thousands per minute on a Dedicated pool sized appropriately. For hosted, it's more bursty.
[05:42] Clara: Security again — audit logs and SSO. We need RBAC so non-engineers can't call production models.
[05:48] Jordan: Redwood Console supports RBAC, token-level audit logs, and per-route dashboards. We'll attach screenshots in the deck.
[05:55] Aisha: Cost is the big tie breaker. Can you ballpark cost for 2M vectors with ~200 qps?
[06:02] Jordan: Rough ballpark depends on your rerank strategy and whether you host embedding generation. For a hybrid rerank and Dedicated instance, customers similar size see $X—Y per month (Jordan mumbles numbers, transcription error) — I'll send detailed pricing; better to run a benchmark to get accurate numbers.
[06:16] Tom: We can share sample dataset (product catalog + click logs) — around 500k core docs now, with 2M total vectors including query history. We'll sanitize and share S3 link.
[06:27] Aisha: Timeline — we want a pilot in 4—6 weeks and then a pilot benchmark. Is that reasonable?
[06:33] Riley: Totally. Typical flow: discovery -> technical deep dive -> pilot (2 weeks benchmark) -> production rollout. For pilot we can use Hosted or Dedicated depending on your security needs; many customers start Hosted for speed then migrate.
[06:45] Clara: If we go Dedicated, how long to provision?
[06:48] Jordan: Provisioning Dedicated can be 2—4 weeks depending on capacity and contracts; Private on-prem is longer. Hosted is immediate.
[06:55] Tom: For the rerank endpoint — API contract? We need a batch endpoint to send top-K candidates and get scores back.
[07:02] Riley: Yes we have a rerank endpoint that accepts candidate lists and returns scores or reordered results; supports streaming responses and tool-calls for structured outputs. We'll send the API spec.
[07:15] Aisha: Excellent. Any limitations on top-K? Sending 100 candidates is fine?
[07:20] Riley: Yes 100 is fine; if you need more we can discuss optimizations. Keep in mind cost scales with how many tokens the cross-encoder processes — if you pass full documents it increases token counts. Many customers only pass snippets.
[07:33] Jordan: Quick note — we also integrate with Redis for hybrid retrieval (storing small dense indexes + metadata) if you want a cheaper vector store option.
[07:40] Tom: Good to know.
[07:44] Riley: Any other blockers?
[07:46] Aisha: Data residency — some enterprise clients require EU-only. Can Redwood host dedicated capacity in eu-west?
[07:52] Jordan: Yes, we have region options; Dedicated/Private can be in eu-west. We'll confirm region availability in the follow-up.
[07:59] Clara: Also need SOC2 attestations and penetration test results for security review.
[08:04] Jordan: We'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 report under an NDA link.
[08:09] Riley: I'll also include a short sample integration guide showing pushing embeddings to Pinecone and using our rerank endpoint with minimal code.
[08:16] Aisha: Great.
[08:18] Jordan: Recap / next steps: Jordan sends pricing and security docs; Riley shares benchmark harness and API spec; Montage shares sample dataset by Feb 9; schedule technical deep dive week of Feb 8. Anything to add?
[08:33] Tom: Sounds good.
[08:35] Aisha: Nope. Thanks.
[08:37] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
